title: Integrating 2 Claude Ultra subscriptions on the same project?
author: Post-reality
selftext: Hi, I have been working on my (quite complicated game project) for almost 2 months already. I have a Claude Ultra subscription of which I use Opus 5.5 which defaults to Max for coding (yeah, I know Max isn't useful for most things, but it technically resorts to high reasonings and not max for most tasks). I use separate, even more expensive models, for assets generation (sprites, layers, in-between frames, animation, audio effects, voice), because Claude sucks at those. Currently, I spend some $500-$1000 a month. One bottleneck is that Claude is very slow, and I reach my usage limit usually by around 5 days or so. I would like to buy a second Claude Ultra subscription and integrate it into my workflow, so that I can work 7 days, and also utilize ultra code, so some tasks can be completed faster. But how would that work like, especially regarding context awareness, speeding up work without introducing new bugs?

comments.author: caesium23
comments.body:
Your question doesn't really make sense. If you burn through the tokens on one account in 5 days, then when you run out, swap to the other account and work for another 5 days. Why would this be an issue? You're just changing the batteries. It won't have any real effect on what you're doing.

Also, if you're burning through that many tokens in 5 days, you are probably doing something horribly wrong. I would look at revising your workflow before buying a second subscription.
